title: One audited year, and it is enough
lede: Kozmo never became a public company, so it filed one set of financial statements with the SEC: the IPO registration of March 2000, covering 1997 to 1999. Nothing after December 1999 was ever audited in public. Figures for 2000 and 2001 below come from the press and are marked as such.

blocks.title: 1999, quarter by quarter
blocks.subtitle: Revenue against the three largest operating expenses and the net loss, $ millions.
blocks.source: Unaudited quarterly results in the Form S-1 of March 21, 2000.[^1] The company began in March 1998; quarterly figures for 1998 were not published.

blocks.title: What one order brought in, and what it cost to carry
blocks.subtitle: Derived: quarterly revenue, gross profit and delivery expense divided by the number of orders in the quarter.
blocks.source: Derived from the S-1: orders of 29,231, 44,275, 78,118 and 177,581 in the four quarters of 1999; revenue, gross profit and delivery expense as reported.[^1] The filing says delivery expense is “primarily” payroll for delivery staff. Rent, warehouse staff and marketing are not included, so the full cost of an order was higher.

blocks.title: Cities served: one, then eleven, then none
blocks.subtitle: Markets in operation at the dates a source gives a count.

points.title: New York
points.text: The first distribution center opens in March 1998.[^1]

points.title: five cities
points.text: Seattle, San Francisco, Boston and Washington are added in six months of 1999.[^1]

points.title: the peak
points.text: 11 cities in August and September 2000. The filing had promised at least ten more by year-end.[^1][^14][^15]

points.title: the first retreat
points.text: Houston and San Diego close on January 8, 2001.[^10][^11]

points.title: the end
points.text: All nine remaining markets stop on April 11, 2001.[^3]

blocks.source: 1998 to February 2000: Form S-1.[^1] April 2000: MSNBC, which reported Chicago and Atlanta as newly opened.[^17] 11 cities: Supermarket News and CNN/IDG.[^14][^15] Nine: E-Commerce Times and The Register.[^10][^11] The count of eight in April 2000 is derived (six plus two).
